root_causes.description: Requests to the payment service are being aborted before completing: payment server-span request rate collapsed to near zero (max 0.038 req/s) while error spans, latency, CPU, and pod health all remained nominal. Aborted requests never produce completed server spans, which explains the traffic collapse without any error/latency/resource anomaly.

evidence.observed_value: request_rate mean=0.010, p95=0.038, max=0.038 req/s across the incident window
evidence.expected_baseline: request_rate ~5-10 req/s under load-generator traffic; near-zero traffic indicates requests aborted before server spans complete

evidence.observed_value: error_rate mean=0.000, p95=0.000, max=0.000 (no error server spans recorded)
evidence.expected_baseline: error_rate < 0.01; absence of error spans combined with traffic collapse indicates aborts occur before span completion
p99 < 100ms; normal latency rules out high_latency fault

evidence.observed_value: cpu_usage mean=0.007, max=0.007 cores (flat, no spike)
evidence.expected_baseline: cpu_usage < 0.5 cores; no spike rules out cpu_stress

evidence.observed_value: Only routine events: 'Updated: Successfully update ObservedGeneration and FailedMessage of resource (count=1)'; no OOMKilled, BackOff, or crash events
evidence.expected_baseline: No crash/kill events expected; rules out pod_crash and memory_stress

evidence.observed_value: [no traces found] - no error traces recorded for payment
evidence.expected_baseline: 0 error traces under normal operation; consistent with aborts preventing span completion

root_causes.description: Checkout depends directly on payment (topology: checkout → payment), so payment aborts propagate as checkout-side payment call failures. However, checkout recorded no error server spans and no error traces in this window, so this is a secondary propagation effect rather than the origin.

evidence.observed_value: error_rate mean=0.000, p95=0.000, max=0.000 for checkout during the window
evidence.expected_baseline: error_rate < 0.01; no checkout-side error propagation observed in this window

evidence.observed_value: [no traces found] - no error traces recorded for checkout
[no logs found] - no payment-related error logs from checkout in the window
evidence.expected_baseline: No payment-related errors expected under normal operation

root_causes.description: Considered and largely ruled out: payment pod events show only routine controller updates with no restarts, OOMKills, or crash-loop backoff, and CPU usage remained flat and low. Retained as a low-confidence fallback only because no direct abort-span evidence was captured.

evidence.observed_value: No OOMKilled/BackOff/FailedMount events; only 'Updated: Successfully update ObservedGeneration and FailedMessage of resource (count=1)'
evidence.expected_baseline: Crash loops would show BackOff/OOMKilled events; none present

evidence.observed_value: cpu_usage mean=0.007, max=0.007 cores (flat, no spike)
evidence.expected_baseline: cpu_usage < 0.5 cores; flat usage inconsistent with crash-loop restart churn

remediation_steps: Inspect and disable the HTTP abort fault injection targeting the payment service (check flagd feature flags / chaos-injection configuration for the abort rule).
Rollout/restart the payment deployment to clear any injected abort state: kubectl rollout restart deployment/payment -n otel-demo.
Verify recovery by confirming payment server request rate returns to baseline (~5-10 req/s) and checkout order completion succeeds.
Add alerting on payment request-rate collapse (e.g., request_rate < 1 req/s for 5 minutes) and on checkout→payment call errors to catch abort faults faster.
Review payment service logs and middleware for abort/short-circuit handlers once log retention covers the window.
